question: 'The Great Indian Novel’ is written by _____ in which he based ‘The Mahabharata’ as a framework for his satirical novel.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shashi Tharoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"The Great Indian Novel" **by **Shashi Tharoor,** published in 1989 by **Viking Press,** is a satirical masterpiece. This fictional work cleverly reimagines the epic Mahabharata within the backdrop of the Indian Independence Movement and the ensuing years.
 
• Tharoor's narrative is rich with puns and references to renowned literary works on India, including those by Rudyard Kipling, Paul Scott, and E. M. Forster.
 
• Structured akin to the Mahabharata, the novel is divided into sections and chapters that mirror the organization of the epic.
 
• Each segment skillfully alludes to themes and events from its counterpart in the Mahabharata, lending depth and complexity to the narrative.
 
• With 18 "books" akin to the 18 books of the Mahabharata and the 18-day Battle of Kurukshetra, Tharoor masterfully weaves together history, mythology, and satire in this remarkable work. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Shashi Tharoor **is a multifaceted Indian personality, renowned for his diverse roles as an international civil servant, diplomat, bureaucrat, politician, and prolific writer.
 
• Representing Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, he has served as a Member of Parliament since 2009 and currently chairs the Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilizers.
 
• Tharoor's illustrious career includes his tenure as an Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations and a notable bid for the position of Secretary-General in 2006.
 
• He is also the Founder-Chairman of the All India Professionals Congress and has held prominent positions such as Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs and Information Technology.
 
• Recognized as a "Global Leader of Tomorrow" by the World Economic Forum, Tharoor has authored around two dozen titles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khushwant Singh**, an Indian luminary, distinguished himself as an author, lawyer, diplomat, journalist, and politician. His seminal work, "Train to Pakistan," published in 1956, is deeply rooted in his experiences during the tumultuous 1947 Partition of India and remains his most celebrated novel.
 
• **Sarojini Naidu, **another prominent figure in Indian history, was a trailblazing political activist and poet. She made history as the first Governor of the United Provinces post-India's independence and played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement, rallying against the British Raj with her eloquent poetry and unwavering determination.
 
• **Kuldip Nayar**, an influential Indian journalist, syndicated columnist, and human rights activist, left an indelible mark with his insightful commentary and fearless advocacy. His extensive career spanned roles as an author, former High Commissioner of India to the United Kingdom, and a notable left-wing political commentator, earning him widespread respect and admiration.
